findings: ers_isOpenEmbedding_proj_of_eqOn (Causal/ErsEtaleMghd.lean:716): its hypotheses force A = U₁ ∩ U₂ on every background (Causal.ers_coe_eq_inter_of_eqOn). The overlap is connected by ers_isPreconnected_inter_of_eqOn, and A is a non-empty open subset of it that is closed in it (hclosed). So the gluing in that theorem is always the trivial one, along the whole overlap, and π is an open embedding by EtaleGluing.isOpenEmbedding_proj with no causal input; the theorem's content is the connectedness of the overlap. Its witness therefore has A = ]-1, 1[ = U₁ ∩ U₂, as every witness must; a witness with a proper A cannot exist in any model.

ers_isPreconnected_inter_of_eqOn (:675) on the line: two developments of a preconnected S always have a preconnected overlap, for any causalities (Causality.real_isPreconnected_inf_of_isCauchySurfaceOn, Causal/ErsWitnesses.lean:147). The witness shows that every hypothesis holds jointly with a proper overlap (neither domain contains the other), but on ℝ the conclusion already follows from hd₁, hd₂ and hSc. No ETT-layer model of the library makes the agreement hypothesis necessary (every other hypothesis holding, a disagreement, a disconnected overlap). Argued, not formalized: on a circle a causal Cm excludes such a model. A point of the far component of the overlap is reached from S along both arcs, by a cau u₁-curve in U₁ and a cau u₂-curve in U₂, both Cm-causal, so either two of its points are Cm-related both ways or S is not Cm-acausal. In 1+1 dimensions one model would be two thin slanted needles over S = {t = 0} that cross above a thin slab, where the cone of cau u at a point is a function of u there, tilted in opposite directions inside Minkowski's cone on the two needles. Such a model is beyond the library's ETT-layer causalities. It also shows that the abstract subluminal setting (sol arbitrary) does not give ERS Cor 4.71's global uniqueness (ghd_02_19.tex:959) without a local uniqueness input.

ers_corollary_4_68_etale (:616) asks for a development of U₁ only, so the line witnesses it with the roadmap's data: U₂ = ]-1, 1[ ∪ ]2, 3[, a development for no causality (ErsWitness.not_isCauchySurfaceOn_disU₂). The paper's statement (ghd_02_19.tex:921–923) has two GHDs and a connected S, and in that reading the hypotheses have no instance on ℝ for any causalities (Causal.real_eqOn_inter_of_isDevelopment: the solutions agree on the overlap). This is the étale counterpart of ErsWitnesses' real_ers_corollary_4_68_agree.

With S disconnected the paper's two-development shape is realised on the line (S = {0, 3}, twoU₁, twoU₂, twoA, disagreement at 3/2 in the component ]5/4, 7/4[ of the overlap). The étale development of ers_theorem_3_45_etale (:587) then has a doubled point: E is Hausdorff, two-piece and causal, the lift of {0, 3} is Cauchy, π is not injective, and the glued solution does not descend. Causal/ErsEtaleMghd.lean:95–99 (SCOPE, 'Witness') is right as written ('no two developments of {0} on the line have' a disconnected overlap), but the obstruction is the connectedness of S, not the line.

kb_proposals: On the timelike line {c} is a Cauchy surface of every bounded ]a, b[ ∋ c (Causal.timelikeLine_isCauchySurfaceOn_Ioo_of_mem: kb/0308's lemma translated by timelikeLine_isCausalIso_addRight and IsCausalIso.isCauchySurfaceOn_image), and {s, t} is one of ]a, b[ ∪ ]c, d[ when a < s < b ≤ c < t < d (timelikeLine_isCauchySurfaceOn_union_Ioo); both are in CausalScaffold.ErsEtaleMghdWitnesses and need no import of Causal.ErsSCWitnesses.

Causal.ErsSCWitnesses reaches Causal.CExtConnexeCauchy.SubArc through CExtConnexeCauchy.Basic, so its isCauchySurfaceOn_Ioo_center and twoIntervals cannot be used by a module that must avoid SubArc; use timelikeLine_isCauchySurfaceOn_Ioo_of_mem and timelikeLine_isCauchySurfaceOn_union_Ioo instead.

A doubled point of the étale development on the line needs a disconnected S: ErsEtaleWitness.timelikeLine_ers_theorem_3_45_etale_twoPoint has S = {0, 3}. With S preconnected, Causal.real_eqOn_inter_of_isDevelopment excludes it for every causality.
A witness of ers_isOpenEmbedding_proj_of_eqOn necessarily has A = U₁ ∩ U₂ (ers_coe_eq_inter_of_eqOn); do not look for one with a proper common development.

(2) ers_isOpenEmbedding_proj_of_eqOn's docstring now says its hypotheses force A = U₁ ∩ U₂ (ers_coe_eq_inter_of_eqOn), so it says nothing of gluing along a proper common development. (3) ErsEtaleMghd's '6-witness' list and SCOPE witness bullet name the new witnesses, and note that 4.68 étale asks only (U₁, u₁) and no connected S, and that a doubled point needs a disconnected S. (4) findings[2]'s 'no instance on ℝ for any causalities' holds with hA and hclosed (or in the paper's PDE setting) only: without them, U₁ = U₂ = ]-1,1[ with u₂ the indicator of ]1/2,1[ gives two developments of {0} disagreeing on a connected overlap; the Lean declaration and SCOPE are precise.
